chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Jamilah from Aban ibn Taghlib said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman, and she did not remain with him after being presented to him for more than four months until she gave birth to a girl. He denied her child, and she claimed that she had become pregnant from him. He said: 'That is not accepted from her, and if they refer the matter to the ruler, they will perform li'an (oath of mutual imprecation), and they will be separated, and she will never be permissible to him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a husband denies paternity of a child born shortly after marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the ruling of *li'an* when a husband denies paternity of a child born within four months of marriage, a period considered too short for typical gestation. The Imam specifies that if the matter goes to court, the mutual oaths are administered, resulting in permanent separation (*la ta'ud*) rather than a simple divorce, emphasizing the finality of this judicial mechanism in Shia jurisprudence.
